issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell does not itself constitute a transfer of land or create an interest in land for the purpose of the statutory restriction on transfers.
material_facts: The parties executed agreements to sell a share in land, and the purchaser sought specific performance.
The court found that the agreements did not themselves create an interest in the land and that the secured dues to the Land Development Bank had been repaid.
issues.conclusion: The agreements were not barred as transfers under Section 48(d) of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, and the purchaser could seek specific performance by proving the agreements’ terms.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, an agreement to sell does not itself create an interest in immovable property or amount to a sale; it enables the intending purchaser to claim specific performance on proving the agreement. The court relied on this distinction and also noted that the secured dues had been repaid. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.specific_performance_dispute: A party brought a dispute seeking enforcement of an agreement to sell land.
predicates.agreement_only_promises_future_sale: The parties made an agreement for a future sale rather than completing a sale.
predicates.agreement_does_not_create_land_interest: The agreement did not itself give the prospective purchaser an interest in the land.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance dispute concerns an agreement that only promises a future sale and creates no land interest, the agreement is not treated as a transfer.

issues.legal_issue: A factual finding on readiness and willingness supported by the first appellate court’s assessment of the evidence cannot be disturbed in a second appeal.
material_facts: The first appellate court considered the pleadings and oral and documentary evidence and found that the purchaser was ready and willing to perform the contract.
The High Court affirmed that finding in the second appeal.
issues.conclusion: The finding on readiness and willingness was a finding of fact that could not be disturbed in the second appeal and was properly affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: A finding of fact made by the first appellate court after considering the evidence is binding in a second appeal and cannot be disturbed merely by reappreciating that evidence. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal from a first appellate decision.
predicates.first_appellate_court_found_readiness_af: The first appellate court found a party ready and willing to perform after assessing the evidence.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, when the first appellate court has found readiness after assessing the evidence, that finding is not disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation plea that was not raised in the trial court or first appellate court and presents a mixed question of law and fact cannot be examined for the first time in a second appeal.
material_facts: The limitation plea had not been raised before either the trial court or the first appellate court.
The plea involved a mixed question of law and fact.
issues.conclusion: The limitation plea could not be examined for the first time in the second appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A mixed question of law and fact that was not raised in the lower courts cannot be examined for the first time in a second appeal. The High Court referred to the Limitation Act, 1963, but the Supreme Court did not decide the limitation issue on its merits. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal from decisions of lower courts.
predicates.limitation_issue_not_raised_in_lower_cou: The party did not raise the limitation issue before the trial court or the first appellate court.
predicates.limitation_issue_is_mixed_question_of_la: Deciding the limitation issue requires consideration of both law and facts.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, a limitation issue that was not raised below and depends on both law and facts is not examined for the first time.

issues.legal_issue: A mixed question of law and fact that was not pleaded or raised in the lower courts cannot be raised for the first time in an appeal under special leave.
material_facts: The party invoked a statutory restriction on transfers for the first time in the Supreme Court appeal.
The party had not raised that plea before the trial court, the first appellate court, or the High Court, and had not laid a foundation for it in the pleadings.
The plea was a mixed question of law and fact.
issues.conclusion: The party could not raise the statutory-restriction plea for the first time in the appeal under Article 136.
issues.legal_principle: A party must lay a foundation in the pleadings for a plea, particularly when it is a mixed question of law and fact. The Supreme Court, as the last appellate court, declined to permit such a plea to be raised for the first time under Article 136 of the Constitution. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and issue_not_raised_in_lower_courts and no_pleading_foundation_for_issue and issue_is_mixed_question_of_law_and_fact

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal brought under special leave to the Supreme Court.
predicates.issue_not_raised_in_lower_courts: The party did not raise the issue before the trial court, the first appellate court, or the High Court.
predicates.no_pleading_foundation_for_issue: The party did not set out a factual foundation for the issue in the pleadings.
predicates.issue_is_mixed_question_of_law_and_fact: Deciding the issue requires consideration of both law and facts.

issues.definition: In an appeal under special leave, an issue not raised below, lacking a pleading foundation and involving both law and fact is not considered for the first time.

issues.legal_issue: A factual contention that an agreement to sell was actually security for a loan cannot be examined in the Supreme Court appeal when it was not urged in the High Court.
material_facts: The party contended in the Supreme Court that the agreements were security for a loan rather than agreements for sale.
The contention concerned a question of fact and had not been urged before the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to examine whether the agreements were security for a loan.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to consider a factual question that had not been urged before the High Court. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal before the Supreme Court.
predicates.contention_is_factual: The contention depends on determining what the parties intended or did as a matter of fact.
predicates.contention_not_urged_in_high_court: The party did not present the contention to the High Court.

issues.definition: In a Supreme Court appeal, a factual contention not urged in the High Court is not examined.
